~news: Elmbridge set out with five fighters under arms and pressed toward Brookley, a neighboring village at dawn. The townsfolk of Brookley held firm, but their walls were thin and their purse light. At nightfall, Elmbridge had taken five houses and ten souls from Brookley, leaving the town with ten fewer souls and five fewer houses than before. Your settlement grows, but the war is not over—every chief watches the numbers, and every purse counts. If you rise with coin and men, you may call allies; if you waver, the raid may come again. The villages around you feel the rhythm of the march, and soon they will decide whether to trade, flee, or fight back.
